author: haiku
reason: B rests on two ideas a newcomer can follow from start to finish: a transactional outbox with a relay that runs in both directions, and a single control row as the switch. Its phases read step by step. A asks the reader to hold many separate pieces at once (heartbeats, flag propagation, gates, forward and reverse sweepers, three coverage paths, counter juggling), and its overview points ahead to step numbers before they are introduced. B does have a few small slips: a wrong cross-reference (7.1 where it means 6.1) and a reference to Redis that a newcomer has no context for.
